findings.claim: The two columns are appended to the default trades frame unconditionally, so a default re-run of any recorded config now writes a trades.csv.gz whose bytes (header + 2 columns) differ from the recorded file; the one in-repo byte-level reproduction script, research/IDX_CAUSAL_CAPACITY_v1/reproduce_a.py (append-only, cannot be edited), would now report trades_csv_identical=false and exit 1 if re-run.
findings.evidence: reproduce_a.py:54-58 compares out['trades'].to_csv(index=False, float_format='%.10g') byte-for-byte with results/runs/20261008T000401Z_MOONSHOT_E1_D1_v1.1/trades.csv.gz, whose header is the 12 original columns (zcat | head -1). Its recorded reproduce_a.json (reproduced: true) is untouched. e3.run_reproduce / e4.run_reproduce (the Stage-0 pattern E5 clones) compare summary stats only (signals, scored, avg net, matched mean) and are unaffected; summary.json and random_draws.csv are byte-identical to ae2cbee on three synthetic configurations (compare_base.py re-run by me: RESULT OK; backtest_base.py sha d969def8... == git show ae2cbee:idx-signals/idxsig/backtest.py). The protocol draft (matched_controls.paired_statistic) explicitly asks for 'new additive trades.csv columns ... in backtest.run', so this is the specified design rather than a defect; it is recorded here because the standing rule says new behaviour is opt-in and the builder's evidence compares trades only 'on the original 12 columns'.
findings.fix: Either accept as specified by the protocol draft and note in research/E5/protocol.json that trades.csv.gz of E5-era runs carries 14 columns (and that reproduce_a.py's byte check is superseded by the stats-only Stage-0 check), or gate the two columns behind an opt-in RunConfig field (e.g. control_means: bool = False, set True by e5.py). Note the opt-in route adds a key to summary['config'] via asdict(cfg), which is itself an additive change to summary.json; the current design keeps summary.json byte-identical. Orchestrator's call; not blocking.

findings.claim: paired_excess returns a non-degenerate-looking p_one_sided when n_clusters == 1 (or very few): with one cluster every resample equals the sample mean, so p is the floor 1/(1+resamples) whenever mean_excess > 0 and ci95 collapses to a point.
findings.evidence: Verified: frame with signal_date ['a','a','a'], net [0.1,-0.2,0.3], control 0 -> n_clusters 1, mean_excess 0.0667, p_one_sided 0.0196 (=1/51 at resamples=50), ci95 [0.0667, 0.0667]. The protocol's gates (debounced flags >= 200, scored >= 200) make this unreachable in practice, and the dict exposes n_clusters so e5.py can guard; no numeric error (counts sum is always >= 1, division safe).
findings.fix: Optional: in paired_excess set p_one_sided and ci95 to None when n_clusters < 2 (keep mean_excess), or have e5.py refuse to judge a gate on a result with n_clusters below a pre-registered minimum. Additive; no default changes.
